trophies.significance: Inaugural T20 World Cup title; Dhoni's first ICC tournament as captain; ignited India's T20 revolution.
Historic ODI tri-series victory in Australia, cementing youthful Indian white-ball era.
India became the No. 1 ranked Test team for the first time in history under Dhoni's leadership.
First Asia Cup title for India in 15 years.
CSK completed double of IPL + CLT20 in same calendar year.
India's 2nd World Cup win after 28 years. Dhoni hit iconic winning six (91* off 79 balls, Player of the Match).
First team in IPL history to successfully defend their title.
Dhoni became the only captain in cricket history to win all three major ICC white-ball trophies (T20 WC, CWC, CT).
Second CLT20 title for CSK; Suresh Raina 109* & Dhoni 23*.
6th Asia Cup title for India; Dhoni finished match with 20* off 6 balls.
'The Comeback Kings' - CSK won IPL title upon returning to the league after a two-year suspension.
CSK's 4th IPL title in Dhoni's 300th match as T20 captain.
Record-equaling 5th IPL title for CSK; dramatic last-ball thriller at 3:00 AM.

iconic_moments.context: Promoted to No. 3 by Sourav Ganguly
Chasing 299, promoted to No. 3 after Tendulkar fell in 1st over
iconic_moments.performance: 183* runs (145 balls, 15 fours, 10 sixes) - Highest ODI score by a wicketkeeper
iconic_moments.result: India won by 6 wickets with 23 balls to spare

iconic_moments.context: Pakistan needed 13 runs off final over with 1 wicket remaining
iconic_moments.performance: Masterstroke captaincy decision to give 20th over to Joginder Sharma; Misbah caught by Sreesanth

iconic_moments.context: CSK needed 16 runs off final over from Irfan Pathan to qualify for semi-finals
iconic_moments.performance: Dhoni hit 4, 2, 6, 6 (54* off 29 balls) followed by helmet punch celebration

iconic_moments.context: India 114/3 chasing 275; Dhoni promoted himself ahead of Yuvraj Singh to counter Muralitharan
iconic_moments.performance: 91* (79 balls, 8 fours, 2 sixes) culminating in iconic match-winning six into the Mumbai night sky

iconic_moments.context: India trailing in 1st innings; counter-attacking double century against Pattinson & Lyon
iconic_moments.performance: 224 runs (265 balls, 24 fours, 6 sixes) - Highest Test score by an Indian wicketkeeper

iconic_moments.context: Rain-reduced 20-over final; England cruising at 110/4 needing 20 off 16 balls
iconic_moments.performance: Captaincy gamble bringing back Ishant Sharma (took 2 wickets in 2 balls); sharp stumpings off spinners
iconic_moments.result: India won by 5 runs (Dhoni completes ICC Trophy Trifecta)

iconic_moments.venue: Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain
iconic_moments.context: India 9 wickets down needing 15 runs off the final over from Shaminda Eranga
iconic_moments.performance: 0, 6, 4, 6 to seal the trophy (45* off 52 balls)

iconic_moments.context: Bangladesh needed 2 runs off 3 balls; Hardik Pandya took 2 wickets; 1 needed off final ball
iconic_moments.performance: Dhoni took off right glove beforehand, sprinted 25 meters, and ran out Mustafizur Rahman by inches

iconic_moments.context: CSK 28/4 chasing 162; needed 26 runs in final over from Umesh Yadav
iconic_moments.performance: 84* (48 balls, 5 fours, 7 sixes) scoring 4, 6, 6, 2, 6 (24 runs in 5 balls)
iconic_moments.result: RCB won by 1 run (Single greatest individual T20 chase effort)

milestones.details: ODI debut vs Bangladesh at Chattogram (run out for 0).
148 vs Pakistan at Visakhapatnam in his 5th ODI.
Test debut vs Sri Lanka at Chennai (scored 30).

milestones.milestone: Fastest to ICC No. 1 ODI Batter
milestones.details: Reached World No. 1 ODI ranking in just 42 innings.
Appointed India captain for the inaugural 2007 ICC World T20.
Captained India in 3rd Test vs South Africa at Kanpur (India won by 8 wickets).
Led Chennai Super Kings in their inaugural IPL match vs Kings XI Punjab.
Led India to ICC Test Championship Mace No. 1 ranking for the first time.
Player of the Match in World Cup Final with 91*.
Scored 224 vs Australia in Chennai (highest by an Indian wicketkeeper).
First captain in history to win T20 WC (2007), CWC (2011), and Champions Trophy (2013).
Retired from Test cricket after 90 matches, 4876 runs, and 27 wins as captain.
First wicketkeeper in cricket history to effect 100 stumpings in ODIs.
Became only the 2nd wicketkeeper-batsman (after Sangakkara) to reach 10,000 ODI runs with a 50+ career average.
Captained India for the 200th time vs Afghanistan in Asia Cup at Dubai.
Announced retirement from international cricket ('Consider me as retired from 1929 hrs').
Led CSK to record 5th IPL title in his 250th IPL appearance.
